correctness.rationale: All 0/1 stable-set vertices are subsets of a single part. The scalar F(h)=sum_i(1-h/a_i)_+ decreases continuously from k>2 to zero, determining unique 0<h<max a_i; p_i=(1-h/a_i)_+/2 are nonnegative with sum one. For a size-s subset of class i the exact squared distance to c is B+s(1-2p_i), bounded by B+h with equality precisely for full classes a_i>=h. The center is a convex combination of positive-weight contact vertices, so the variance identity forces every other center y to radius squared at least R^2+||y-c||^2, proving global minimality and uniqueness. Algebra gives h=(|I|-2)/(sum_{i in I}1/a_i), the rational radius, and stability under adding b<=h. Fresh exact rational profiles (1,1,1),(1,2,3,6),(10,10,10,1),(10,10,10,1,1,1) verify contacts and the 20/3 plateau; the symbolic proof is infinite.

value.rationale: The ordinary complete-multipartite stable-set polytope is canonical for perfect-graph/2-level geometry. The theorem determines the unique Euclidean enclosing center, every contact vertex, exact rational active-set rule and invariant plateau on adjoining any number of sufficiently small classes. The threshold and contact geometry are meaningful all-profile statements rather than a routine table or unmotivated finite slice.
